_comment: What each file in the section-05 tree is for. The hand-written half of a generated tree.
Structure comes from the repository and cannot go stale. This cannot be derived, so an
eval asserts every derived path has an entry here — adding a workflow fails CI until
someone says what it is for. That is the same contract annotations.json already has for
the pipeline diagram, and deliberately a separate file: this keys by path and holds
short/detail, that keys by node id and holds lane/stage/cost. Different facts about the
same objects, no field in common, so they cannot contradict each other. [spec 0003 D4-D5]
Written by reading each file. Where a file states its own purpose in a header comment,
the description paraphrases that rather than inventing a second account of it.
`detail` is optional. An entry without one renders as a plain row, not an empty
disclosure. Nothing here is checked for accuracy — only for existence. [spec omissions]

.claude/agents/simplifier.md.short: reduction pass before a pull request
.claude/agents/simplifier.md.detail: Reviews a finished change for needless complexity and removes it. Quality only — it does not hunt for bugs.

.claude/agents/verifier.md.short: runs the checks, reports a verdict
.claude/agents/verifier.md.detail: Has its own context window, so four hundred lines of build output never enter the session doing the implementation.

.claude/hooks/audit.mjs.short: logs what the agent touched, and when
.claude/hooks/audit.mjs.detail: Git records commits and GitHub records approvals; this covers the part nobody otherwise sees. Local only — committing it left the working tree permanently dirty and made git checkout refuse to switch branches.

.claude/hooks/format.mjs.detail: Formatting is not worth a review comment or a turn of the agent's attention. A hook settles it silently and identically every time.

.claude/hooks/guard-bash.mjs.detail: Denies force-push, reset --hard, curl piped to a shell, and writes straight to the default branch. It matches the raw command string, which is why it also refuses prose that quotes those commands.

.claude/hooks/protect-approved.mjs.short: freezes an accepted intent or spec
.claude/hooks/protect-approved.mjs.detail: Once Status says accepted, the artifact stops being editable by an agent. Amending one is a proposal a human installs.

.claude/hooks/protect-guardrails.mjs.short: the agent cannot edit its own guardrails
.claude/hooks/protect-guardrails.mjs.detail: Denies writes to .github/workflows, .claude/settings.json and .claude/hooks. CI workflows define what runs without a human; an agent that can edit them can grant itself new powers.

.claude/settings.json.short: wires the hooks — the agent cannot edit this
.claude/settings.json.detail: Five hooks on two events. It carries no permissions block yet, which is intent 0050: the boundary between what the agent may and may not do is currently a sentence in a skill rather than a list in a file.

.claude/skills/house-style/SKILL.md.short: design and prose constraints for this site
.claude/skills/house-style/SKILL.md.detail: Institutional knowledge applied as a constraint rather than a prompt someone retypes — including the asset-path rule, which exists because that exact bug shipped once.

.claude/skills/intent/SKILL.md.short: Stage 1 — the intent template and its rules
.claude/skills/intent/SKILL.md.detail: States a problem, never a solution. Also holds the id rule: the number is the GitHub issue number, because incrementing from the directory listing produced two 0003s in a day.

.claude/skills/sdlc/SKILL.md.short: the orchestrator — does the stage that is next
.claude/skills/sdlc/SKILL.md.detail: Given an id it reads which artifacts exist and performs the one stage that follows, rather than being told which. --auto runs the remaining stages in one pull request; it may compress agreement, never manufacture it.

.claude/skills/ship/SKILL.md.short: Stage 3 — turning a plan into a pull request
.claude/skills/ship/SKILL.md.detail: What must pass, what the body has to say, and which commands a human needs next.

.claude/skills/spec/SKILL.md.detail: Its most valuable output is not the design but the numbered decisions, because those are what later work cites when it needs to diverge.

.github/workflows/agent-intent.yml.detail: Triggers on labelled, never on opened. Applying a label needs write access, which makes the trigger a maintainer triaging rather than a stranger typing into a box.

.github/workflows/bands.yml.short: cron; a breach opens an issue
.github/workflows/bands.yml.detail: Stage 6, and the step that hands the loop back to a human. It opens the issue and deliberately does not label it: a breach is evidence, not a decision.

.github/workflows/checks.yml.short: format, evals, diagram drift — builds nothing
.github/workflows/checks.yml.detail: The process half of the pipeline, about four seconds. Runs on everything, because a change to docs or .claude can break a hook or an artifact without touching the site.

.github/workflows/claude-code-review.yml.short: reviews a pull request — the expensive one
.github/workflows/claude-code-review.yml.detail: Roughly one run in five actually posts. It skips drafts, bot-authored pull requests, and anything under docs. No turn limit: --max-turns bounded the work rather than the cost and bought nothing twice.

.github/workflows/claude.yml.detail: The one place a stranger's words reach an agent. The action checks the triggering user has write access; that check is a default of the action, not a line in this file.

.github/workflows/deploy.yml.detail: The build job has no credentials. The deploy job has them and cannot start until a named human approves. That asymmetry is the whole governance argument.

.github/workflows/digest.yml.short: Monday: what is in flight, to Slack
.github/workflows/digest.yml.detail: Runs npm run intents, which is a script and not a model — same answer every time, no tokens. Weekly rather than daily, because a digest that arrives every morning becomes wallpaper.

.github/workflows/preview.yml.short: every pull request gets a live URL
.github/workflows/preview.yml.detail: Uses a different FTP account from deploy: its user is chrooted to the preview directory and cannot reach the live site. Environments are about blast radius; approval is a separate axis.

.github/workflows/security.yml.short: npm audit — the agentic half is a stub
.github/workflows/security.yml.detail: A labelled shell, and the site says so. The agent step is written and commented out; a static site has almost no attack surface, and inventing a finding would be the dishonesty this repository argues against.

.github/workflows/verify.yml.short: builds the site, crawls every link
.github/workflows/verify.yml.detail: Stage 4, and the only thing allowed to say it works. Path-filtered to changes that could alter the built output, so editing a spec does not deploy a website.

.nvmrc.detail: Astro refuses Node 20. On the Windows laptop nvm use needs elevation and fails silently, so the PATH is prefixed instead of trusting the switch.

bands.yaml.detail: Availability, page weight and build time. The mechanism is real and the metrics are toy — there are no users, so there is no error rate to watch.

docs/sdlc/0002-navigation-usability/inte.short: the problem, and what would be true once fixed

docs/sdlc/0002-navigation-usability/plan.short: files, order of work, and how completion is proven

docs/sdlc/0002-navigation-usability/spec.short: numbered design decisions and their reasons

evals/run.mjs.detail: Asserts the guardrails still deny what they claim to deny and that generated artifacts keep their shape. No judgement of quality — that is the token-hungry half, and it is labelled as missing.

package.json.short: the commands, including the one that matters
package.json.detail: npm run verify builds, serves at the real base path, crawls every link and runs the evals. A Node script rather than shell glue, because anything with shell in it is a portability bug waiting for a reader on another OS.
